join_order.notes: Single k_id=117 resolved by linear scan of keyword.off/dat with length-23 prefilter. CSR slot yields ~41,840 mk rowids.

join_order.build: t1_ids = distinct mk.movie_id from CSR slot (~41,819 ids)
join_order.notes: Empirical: probing 41,819 t1_ids into ml offsets only hits 540 nonempty ranges producing 4,388 rows. Linear scan of tiny 29,997-row ml is cheaper and cache-friendly (120KB movie_id col) than 41,819 random lookups into 10MB mloff array. Avoids per-t1 offset reads entirely.
Dense PK lookup into title.{off,dat} for t2 string.
link_type has only 18 rows; trivial direct deref.

filters.notes: Length-23 prefilter via koff[i+1]-koff[i]==23 then memcmp. Single match (k_id=117).

data_structures.keyword_scan: sequential_scan with length prefilter on int64 keyword.off
data_structures.t1_ids_set: std::unordered_set<int32_t> reserved to 42000 (or absl::flat_hash_set). Built from CSR rowids→movie_id dereference. Size ~41,819 ints ≈ 168KB payload; hash table ~1MB.
data_structures.ml_scan: sequential mmap read of movie_link/movie_id.bin (120KB) probing t1_ids_set
data_structures.aggregation: three running MIN string variables (lt_link_min, t1_title_min, t2_title_min), compared via lex order on byte ranges; copy bytes to owning std::string only when a new minimum is found

parallelism.notes: Total work is tiny: 134K keyword scan + 42K hash set build + 30K ml linear scan + 4,388 string min comparisons. Thread spawn overhead would exceed kernel time. ml linear scan touches ~120KB; entire working set well under L2.

indexes.purpose: join_lookup: O(1) access to all mk rowids for k_id=117
